policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV explicitly gives Jehovah as the third-person subject in 'he turn it ... and make it gross darkness'; 'make' therefore represents the ketiv third-person form ישית rather than the qere imperative וְשִׁית. The listed notes are alternative renderings or a Hebrew gloss and do not decide the unit.

ASV 'Lift up your eyes' does not mark whether the addressee is plural (qere שְׂאוּ) or feminine singular (ketiv שאי), because English imperative 'lift' and possessive 'your' permit both; no mapped textual-variant note distinguishes them, so the qere remains the base fallback.

ASV 'behold them' does not mark whether the addressee is plural (qere וּרְאוּ) or feminine singular (ketiv וראי), because the English imperative is compatible with both; no mapped textual-variant note distinguishes them, so the qere remains the base fallback.
